newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SEE RISE IN 1996 EARLY DEBT REDEMPTIONS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SEE RISE IN 1996 EARLY DEBT REDEMPTIONS.

text.p: The Dutch Agency of the Ministry of Finance said on Thursday its remaining borrowing requirement for 1996 may rise to about 5.0 billion guilders to fund early redemptions of debt.
The remaining funding task had been 1.8 billion guilders out of a total programme of 35.1 billion for the year, allowing for funds raised up until October 1.

But in its quartely review issued this month, the agency said: "If the interest rate developments are favourable for early redemptions, the remaining borrowing requirement will increase to approximately five billion guilders."
A spokesman for the agency said some private placements of state debt to institutions and public loans would be redeemed early but he was not more specific.
The ministry has previously said it would make no more calls on the capital market in 1996, in view of the projected size of the remaining borrowing programme.
Until October 1, it had raised 33.3 billion guilders on the capital market, of which 5.2 billion was raised in the first quarter to fund early redemptions.
Private placements represent 16 percent of national Dutch debt, with 82 percent of them maturing within five years.
